title: 第二十一章 绑人第二十二章 又一个绝境
lines: 长孙岳从后巷走了出来。
灰白色的长袍，兜帽压得很低。他的脚步极轻，轻得像猫——不，比猫还轻。猫走路还有肉垫触地的细微声响，他没有。他像一道影子，从墙根的阴影中无声无息地滑了出来。
老三察觉到了什么。
他转过身。
灰白色的长袍。兜帽。看不见脸。那个人站在他身后，不到五步。
老三的手猛地攥紧剑柄。
长孙岳没有回答。
他继续往前走。一步，两步，三步。每一步都很慢，慢到老三能看清他衣袍上的每一道褶皱。但每一步都像踩在老三的心口上——压迫感层层递进，像水慢慢没过咽喉。
老三拔出了剑。
短剑上流转着灰色的灵力——灵魂之力。那不是普通的灵力，是直接作用于灵魂的力量，无视肉身防御，无视护体罡气。
他一剑刺出。
灰色的灵力化作一道无形的波纹，直奔长孙岳的眉心。
空气在波纹所过之处微微扭曲——不是被撕裂，是被侵蚀。灵魂攻击，无声，无形，不可阻挡。
长孙岳没有躲。
他硬生生接下了这一击。
无形的波纹撞上他的眉心，像一把无形的刀刺入灵魂深处。
他的身体晃了一下。
然后站稳了。
老三的瞳孔猛然收缩。
他的灵魂攻击，对这个人——几乎没有效果。
不是无效。是对方的灵魂太强了。他的攻击像一把匕首刺向一面铁壁——匕首断了，铁壁上连痕迹都没有留下。灵魂攻击虽然强大，能无视防御，但前提是灵魂强度要高于对手。
长孙岳没有给他喘息的机会。
一掌拍出。
空间撕裂。
掌风所过之处，空气发出尖锐的嘶鸣——不是风的声音，是空间被撕裂的声音。无形的裂缝在掌风前端蔓延，像一张看不见的嘴，张开，咬下。
老三来不及闪避，只能抬手格挡。
掌臂相交。
一声闷响。老三的衣袖被撕碎，手臂上绽开一道血痕——不是被掌风打伤的，是被空间裂缝划伤的。他的身体向后飞去，撞在酒楼的柱子上。
短剑脱手飞出，插在街边的地面里，剑身嗡嗡震颤。
第二掌。
老三的胸口塌了一块。肋骨断裂的声音清晰可闻。他的口中涌出鲜血，染红了灰白色的衣袍。
第三掌。
老三的身体从柱子上弹起，飞过街道，撞在对面的墙上。墙面裂开，蛛网般的裂纹向四周蔓延。
长孙岳走到他面前。
老三瘫坐在墙根下，眼睛还睁着，但光芒已经暗了。他的嘴唇在动，想说什么，却发不出声音——肺被断裂的肋骨刺穿，血堵住了喉咙。
长孙岳的手按在他的头顶。
老三的眼睛死死盯着兜帽下那张看不见的脸。他想知道是谁。他想知道杀他的人是谁。
长孙岳没有给他答案。
长孙岳蹲下身，掌心凝聚出一丝空间之力——无形的，看不见的，但能感觉到。那是一种让皮肤发紧、让毛发竖立的压迫感，像暴风雨来临前的宁静。
一掌拍下。元婴碎裂，化为虚无。
长孙岳站起身。
楼上传来脚步声。慌乱、沉重、没有章法——不像是修士的脚步，倒像是普通人的脚步。
祖昊。
content_en:
Changsun Yue walked out of the back alley.
Gray-white robe with a low hood. His steps were extremely light, as light as a cat—no, lighter than a cat. When a cat walks, there is a subtle sound of pads touching the ground, but he does not. He was like a shadow, sliding out from the shadow of the wall silently.
The third child noticed something.
He turned around.
Off-white robe. hood. No face visible. The man stood not five steps behind him.
The third child's hand suddenly clenched the hilt of the sword.
"Who?"
Changsun Yue did not answer.
He kept walking. One step, two steps, three steps. Every step was slow, so slow that the third child could clearly see every fold in his robe. But every step was like stepping on Lao San's heart - the pressure was increasing layer by layer, like water slowly filling the throat.
The third child drew his sword.
Gray spiritual power - the power of the soul - flows on the dagger. That is not ordinary spiritual power, it is a power that acts directly on the soul, ignoring physical defense and body-protecting aura.
He stabbed out with his sword.
The gray spiritual power turned into an invisible ripple and went straight to Changsun Yue's eyebrows.
The air is slightly distorted wherever the ripples pass—not torn apart, but eroded. Soul attack, silent, invisible, unstoppable.
Changsun Yue did not hide.
He took the blow forcefully.
Invisible ripples hit his forehead, like an invisible knife piercing the depths of his soul.
His body swayed.
Then stood firm.
The third child's pupils suddenly contracted.
"You——"
His soul attack had almost no effect on this man.
Not invalid. It's because the other party's soul is too strong. His attack was like a dagger piercing an iron wall - the dagger broke, leaving no trace on the iron wall. Although the soul attack is powerful and can ignore defense, the premise is that the soul strength is higher than the opponent.
Changsun Yue didn't give him a chance to breathe.
Clap it with one palm.
Space is torn apart.
Wherever the wind passed by, the air made a sharp scream—not the sound of wind, but the sound of space being torn apart. Invisible cracks spread at the front of the palm, like an invisible mouth, opening and biting down.
The third child had no time to dodge, so he could only raise his hands to block.
The palms of the arms meet.
There was a muffled sound. The third child's sleeves were torn to pieces, and a bloodstain opened on his arm - not from the wind of the palm, but from the cracks in space. His body flew backwards and hit the pillar of the restaurant.
The dagger flew out of his hand and was stuck in the ground on the street, the blade buzzing and trembling.
The second palm.
The third child's chest collapsed. The sound of ribs breaking was clearly audible. Blood gushed out of his mouth, staining his gray-white robes red.
The third palm.
The third child's body bounced off the pillar, flew across the street, and hit the opposite wall. The wall cracked, and spiderweb-like cracks spread around.
Changsun Yue walked up to him.
The third child sat slumped under the wall, his eyes still open, but the light had dimmed. His lips were moving, trying to say something, but no sound came out - his lungs were pierced by broken ribs, and blood blocked his throat.
Changsun Yue put his hand on the top of his head.
The third child's eyes were fixed on the invisible face under the hood. He wanted to know who it was. He wants to know who killed him.
Changsun Yue didn't give him an answer.
Changsun Yue squatted down and condensed a trace of space power in his palm - invisible and invisible, but he could feel it. It was a pressure that made the skin tighten and the hair stand on end, like the calm before the storm.
Clap it with one palm. The Nascent Soul shattered into pieces and turned into nothingness.
Changsun Yue stood up.
There were footsteps upstairs. Panic, heavy, and disorganized—not like the steps of a monk, but like the steps of an ordinary person.
Zu Hao.
